name: Osimertinib
drug_class: EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (third generation, irreversible)

discovery.note: A mono-anilino-pyrimidine designed to covalently target mutant EGFR including the T790M resistance mutation while sparing wild-type EGFR.

tagline: Third-generation EGFR inhibitor that overcomes T790M and penetrates the brain
summary: Osimertinib is an irreversible EGFR inhibitor that selectively targets sensitising EGFR mutations and the T790M resistance mutation, with good central nervous system penetration. It is the standard first-line treatment for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer and is also approved as adjuvant therapy after surgery and after chemoradiation for stage III disease.
mechanism: Osimertinib's acrylamide warhead forms a covalent bond with cysteine 797 in the EGFR ATP-binding site, irreversibly inhibiting mutant receptors (exon 19 deletion, L858R and T790M) with much lower activity against wild-type EGFR, reducing skin and gut toxicity.
The C797S mutation, MET amplification and histological transformation are common mechanisms of resistance.
uses: First-line treatment of metastatic EGFR-mutant NSCLC (alone or with platinum–pemetrexed)
EGFR T790M-positive NSCLC after earlier EGFR inhibitors
Adjuvant therapy after resection of stage IB–IIIA EGFR-mutant NSCLC
Unresectable stage III EGFR-mutant NSCLC after chemoradiation

history.title: Candidate selected
history.detail: AZD9291 nominated after a structure-based programme begun in 2009.

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA approves osimertinib for T790M-positive NSCLC, under three years after first-in-human dosing.

history.title: AURA3
history.detail: Full approval after superiority over platinum–pemetrexed in T790M-positive disease.

history.title: FLAURA
history.detail: First-line approval after improved progression-free survival versus gefitinib or erlotinib; overall survival benefit reported in 2019.

history.title: ADAURA
history.detail: Approved as adjuvant therapy after resection of EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

history.title: FLAURA2 and LAURA
history.detail: FDA approves osimertinib with chemotherapy first-line (February) and after chemoradiation for unresectable stage III disease (September).

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A to active metabolites AZ5104 and AZ7550

facts: FDA accelerated approval came less than three years after the first patient was dosed.
